title: Ratio FreeDiver Sapphire Stainless Steel Green Dial Quartz 200M (different colors) $132 Shipped @ RATIO
body:
Deal: Ratio FreeDiver Sapphire Stainless Steel Green Dial Quartz 200M (different colors) $132 Shipped @ RATIO

[Haunt] Everytime I see these budget brands (alongside Erebus, Cestrian, AliX chinese brands etc) using Sapphire at this price point makes me stray away further and further from Seiko with their obsession with Hardlex/Mineral and their ever-increasing RRP
[skibidigrimacmoggr67] AliX Chinese etc
I don't know about the first two you mention. but I think Ratio is similar price as r/Chinesewatches, except slightly better quality and brand name looks better, as in I think short names like Ratio written on the watch looks better than the chinese brands I saw when searching, which were Watchdives and Addiesdive .
[Haunt] Erebus is an Australian microbrand founded by Jody of Just One More Watch (youtube channel) with his partner Steven, while Cestrian is a UK-based Microbrand. Both of them manufactures their watches in China (with San Martin making Erebus, Cestrian not sure) but yeah I agree, basically they are chinese watches but with better branding, brand names and local customer service. But still makes you wonder how much Seiko inflates their watches. One of the reasons their SSK line has put me off for years..
[skibidigrimacmoggr67] ok nice Erebus based in australia good to know.
[tubeidea] basically they are chinese watches but with better branding, brand names and local customer service.
Not that it's worth anything. People have had issues with quality control on their watches, but according to Erebus they were "in spec" or whatever corpospeak they used.
Doesn't help that the watches themselves are boring homages taking many elements of existing watches and doing literally nothing new or interesting. If you're gonna make a microbrand, at least make it unique.
[boozed] @tubeidea: I think the problem microbrands have these days – if they choose not to simply offer slavish copies of existing designs – is that everything interesting and appealing has already been done.
And there are way too many of them.
[Haunt] @tubeidea: Tell me about it. I own an Erebus Ascent 36 and one side of the quick release system on my bracelet doesn't work properly. I have to wiggle it very hard which defeats the purpose of a quick release system. Either the lug hole is wrong, the lug width is a bit shorter or the spring bar itself is faulty. Erebus told me that they haven't had any spring bar issues at all (well, I just told them thats what I thought was faulty so was more of a guess by me) but it was basically the same response as others has had. Just left it as is as I prefer it on bracelet anyway.
But I still think it's a great watch and better spec'd, better finished than an equivalent Seiko at a cheaper price.
[tubeidea] @Haunt:
But I still think it's a great watch and better spec'd, better finished than an equivalent Seiko at a cheaper price.
No doubt. It's just boring. I would just cut out the middleman and go buy a San Martin, you'll probably get better customer support to boot.
[Alcaro] I don't agree on the branding at all. Erebus has about the same authenticity to it as San Martin does to China and equally little to do with watches, time or horology. I found it very grating after Jody chuckled for years at Boderry and San Martin goofiness that Erebus was the naming homework he turned in along with a butthole logo.
[Jimothy Wongingtons] @Alcaro: It almost seemed like a joke … which surprisingly picked up steam
[Haunt] @Alcaro:
butthole logo
Ha, ngl that made me chuckle. Can't unsee it now, darn you! lol
Eh, to each his own I guess. Perhaps i'm just a bit biased because I like Jody and his channel a lot, and also got mine for half the price used in brand new condition so it's an excellent value proposition for me
[Alcaro] @Haunt: I like Jody a lot too, and I was looking forward to dipping my toes into microbrands with his effort if I liked what I saw. Alas…
Still, I don't think I could have passed up the deal you found even if it was winking at me uncomfortably—Good find!
[garage sale] Hardles vs sapphire, reason is sapphire is strong but brittle and hitting something hard underwater is a risk, l personally prefer saphire for my desk divers as its more scratch resistant , but the watches I take diving seem to come as hardlex , not my choice, manufacturer.
[skibidigrimacmoggr67] I was just recommended the video on the Speed Razer again and noticed something you can't see from the picture so I thought I should mention it.
the glass on the speed racer is 3D bubble glass (curved edge glass) like the apple watch. so it creates slight distortion and is easier to damage (because it sticks out). I personally would not buy a watch even as a gift with 3D glass because of the 2nd thing.
[GRP] I own a Ratio. It gave me the colorway I wanted at a great price and I have been very happy with it. I would buy this watch save I already have the same in a Citizen (with cylcops).
[skibidigrimacmoggr67] since you mention citizen you reminded me.
in a review on youtube, guy said Ratio's "anti reflective coating" on glass matches higher end watches. in that's it's very clear.
they mentioned the coating on many citizen models made the glass "hazy" or something. they said it's hard to describe but the coating depending on its quality can make the glass "less clear".
